coverage: Round-2 finder on the Martin MEASUREMENT angle, continuing a predecessor cut off at 18 sources / 49 claims; this return carries only the 16 new sources and 60 new claims, and the checkpoint file sweep/found-martin-measurement.json carries the merged 34 sources / 109 claims with complete:true (the predecessor's snapshot is preserved at found-martin-measurement.seed.json). NAMED ROSTER: Spathis — FETCHED by the predecessor, with adverb scarcity and dropped -ly already counted separately in its claims. Ben Blatt, Nabokov's Favorite Word Is Mauve, 'Use Sparingly' — FETCHED snippet-only through Google Books SearchWithinVolume2 (volume 0AhHDgAAQBAJ, recovered via books?vid=ISBN9781501105388 after the Books API daily quota was exhausted): Blatt's corpus does include eight Martin novels and Martin is one of his fifty example authors, his cinnamon words are dragons, cloaks and unsullied, but a full-text search returns his name on no page of the Use Sparingly chapter, so that chapter appears to print no Martin adverb figure. David J. Peterson, The Art of Language Invention (2015) — FETCHED in full as archive.org OCR text, and it answers the angle's question outright: fifty-six Dothraki words and names in the first three books, twenty-four of them proper names, and six High Valyrian words. dothraki.com — FETCHED by the predecessor. WordsRated chapter-length figures — the roster URL wordsrated.com/a-song-of-ice-and-fire-statistics/ is NOT FOUND (404); the live game-of-thrones-stats page the predecessor read carries only per-book chapter totals, so chapter length was covered instead from the A Song of Ice and Fire Wiki's chapter-by-chapter table (shortest 1,696 words, longest 7,334) and a reader's per-volume page average on asoiaf.westeros.org. BLOCKED: the Ukrainian archaism study at apiph.eenu.edu.ua (host unreachable); prosecraft.io itself (dead, only its A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms page survives in the Wayback Machine, its percentile pages archived only as 301/302); iceandfire.fandom.com and wordsrated.com live behind Cloudflare/WAF, both recovered through Wayback raw captures; hub.lexile.com and asearchoficeandfire.com are JavaScript-only. EXPANSION — 11 new substantive sources across the three routes: bibliography chasing gave the Shaxpir methodology post behind prosecraft and the LightSail and TeachingBooks text-complexity records; lateral searches gave the archived prosecraft book page, AutoCrit's measurement of A Game of Thrones, the Books & Boots affix-and-compound essay, the ASOIAF Wiki chapter table and the westeros.org chapter-length thread; and a GitHub repository search gave the find of the round, a complete scrape of the prosecraft library (22,449 books) carrying figures for nine Martin titles including Fire and Blood, which lets the maester-chronicle register be compared numerically with the novels for the first time in this sweep. OpenAlex and Semantic-Scholar-shaped searches for Martin stylometry returned nothing beyond what the predecessor already had, and two consecutive lateral searches surfaced nothing new, so discovery stopped.
